evals.name: Shipwright build setup
evals.prompt: Generate a Shipwright Build and ClusterBuildStrategy for a Go application called 'inventory-svc'. Use Buildah as the build strategy with multi-stage support. The source is at https://github.com/acme-corp/inventory-svc.git (branch main). Push the built image to quay.io/acme/inventory-svc with a tag based on the Git SHA. Include registry auth via a Secret reference. Set a 20-minute timeout and retention limits.
expectations: Output contains kind: ClusterBuildStrategy with apiVersion: shipwright.io/v1beta1
ClusterBuildStrategy uses Buildah (image reference contains buildah)
Output contains kind: Build with apiVersion: shipwright.io/v1beta1
Build has spec.source.type: Git with url: https://github.com/acme-corp/inventory-svc.git
Build has spec.strategy referencing the ClusterBuildStrategy by name
Build output image is quay.io/acme/inventory-svc with a dynamic tag (not :latest)
Build output has pushSecret or credentials.name referencing a registry auth Secret
Build has spec.timeout set to 20m or equivalent duration
Build has spec.retention with succeededLimit and failedLimit values
ClusterBuildStrategy step includes resource limits for CPU and memory

evals.name: Tekton CI pipeline
evals.prompt: Create a complete Tekton CI pipeline called 'webapp-ci' for a Node.js application. The pipeline should have 5 tasks in order: git-clone, test (npm test), build (using Shipwright BuildRun), scan (Trivy vulnerability scanner with HIGH,CRITICAL severity), and gitops-update (commit new image tag to a GitOps repo at https://github.com/acme-corp/gitops-config.git). Include proper workspaces for source code and credentials. Create the ServiceAccount with registry push and Git write secrets.
expectations: Output contains kind: Pipeline with apiVersion: tekton.dev/v1
Pipeline has exactly 5 tasks: git-clone, test, build, scan, gitops-update
Tasks are ordered with proper runAfter dependencies forming a sequential chain
Pipeline defines workspaces for shared source and credentials
git-clone task uses a ClusterTask or Task reference for git-clone
scan task references Trivy scanner with severity parameter set to HIGH,CRITICAL
gitops-update task commits the new image tag to the GitOps repo
Output includes a ServiceAccount with secrets for registry and Git access
ServiceAccount has a RoleBinding scoped to the namespace (not cluster-admin)
Pipeline params include repo-url, revision, and image-tag

evals.name: Tekton Triggers with EventListener
evals.prompt: Set up Tekton Triggers for a GitHub webhook on push events. Create an EventListener called 'github-push-listener' in namespace 'ci' that receives GitHub push webhooks, extracts the repo URL, branch, and commit SHA from the payload, and triggers the 'webapp-ci' Pipeline. Include: a TriggerBinding that maps GitHub webhook fields (body.repository.clone_url, body.ref, body.after) to parameters, a TriggerTemplate that creates a PipelineRun referencing the webapp-ci Pipeline with those parameters, the EventListener with a GitHub interceptor that validates the webhook secret and filters for push events only, a ServiceAccount for the EventListener with RBAC to create PipelineRuns, and a Secret for the GitHub webhook token.
expectations: Output contains kind: EventListener with apiVersion: triggers.tekton.dev/v1beta1
EventListener has a trigger with a GitHub interceptor
GitHub interceptor has a secretRef for webhook token validation
GitHub interceptor filters for push events (eventTypes contains push)
Output contains kind: TriggerBinding with apiVersion: triggers.tekton.dev/v1beta1
TriggerBinding maps body.repository.clone_url, body.ref, and body.after to parameters
Output contains kind: TriggerTemplate with apiVersion: triggers.tekton.dev/v1beta1
TriggerTemplate creates a PipelineRun referencing the webapp-ci Pipeline
Output includes a ServiceAccount with a RoleBinding granting permissions to create PipelineRuns
Output includes a Secret for the GitHub webhook token

evals.name: Diagnose broken PipelineRun
evals.prompt:
My PipelineRun keeps failing. Here's what I have:

The Pipeline declares 3 workspaces: shared-workspace, docker-credentials, and git-credentials. But my PipelineRun only binds shared-workspace with a VolumeClaimTemplate. The error is: "workspace 'docker-credentials' declared by pipeline not provided by pipelinerun".

Also, inside the Pipeline, the build task creates a Shipwright BuildRun using apiVersion: shipwright.io/v1alpha1. And the gitops-update task has no runAfter field — it might run before the scan task finishes.

What's wrong and how do I fix all the issues?
expectations: Identifies the missing workspace bindings (docker-credentials and git-credentials not bound in PipelineRun)
Provides fix: add workspace entries in PipelineRun for docker-credentials and git-credentials with Secret or VolumeClaimTemplate
Identifies the deprecated apiVersion shipwright.io/v1alpha1 and recommends shipwright.io/v1beta1
Identifies the missing runAfter on gitops-update task causing potential out-of-order execution
Provides fix: add runAfter referencing the scan task to gitops-update
Prioritizes or categorizes the issues by severity (missing workspaces = runtime failure, deprecated API = future breakage, missing runAfter = race condition)
Does NOT just generate new YAML from scratch — actually diagnoses the specific problems described
Provides corrected YAML snippets for each fix

evals.name: Trade-off: Shipwright vs Tekton Buildah task
evals.prompt: We currently use a Tekton Task with Buildah to build container images. Our team lead wants us to switch to Shipwright. We have 15 pipelines that each have a buildah task step. What would we gain from switching to Shipwright, what would break, and should we actually switch? Give me a real recommendation, not just a feature list.
expectations: Lists concrete gains: Build CRD with retention policies, strategy reuse via ClusterBuildStrategy, source-to-image without full pipeline overhead, build-specific timeout and retry semantics
Lists what breaks or requires migration: 15 pipelines need refactoring, BuildRun replaces the buildah TaskRun step, different error handling and status checking
Gives a nuanced recommendation — not a blanket 'yes switch' or 'no stay'
Suggests a migration path (e.g., run both in parallel, migrate one pipeline first as a pilot)
Acknowledges that for teams already working well with Tekton Buildah, the migration cost may not be worth it
Mentions that Shipwright Build can be triggered from within a Tekton Pipeline (they're not mutually exclusive)
Does NOT just list features — actually weighs the tradeoffs for this specific scenario (15 existing pipelines)
